title: fix(doctor): unblock shared-state repair during July upgrades
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes July npm upgrades failing in candidate Doctor before it can record deferred plugin migrations.

## User Impact

Updates from `2026.7.1-2` and `2026.7.1-1` can prepare their older shared database before plugin bookkeeping. Existing data-risk refusals and durable pending-plugin inputs remain protected. This removes the first upgrade blocker; the full survivor matrix still exposes separate post-core completion and retained-session receipt defects owned by the campaign's M2 lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

Candidate Doctor previously attempted a writable pending-plugin record before its shared-schema repair stage, so the July database failed on repairable `audit-events-v2`. Explicit repair preflight now reuses the existing conditional schema step and refusal receipts before those writes. No schema version changes. Plugin-index persistence now owns its existing post-write identity checks, preserving their order and error behavior.

The existing schema transaction remains the recovery boundary. This does not promise a whole-update rollback after a later Doctor failure; package rollback can refuse an incompatible migrated schema.

Maintainer landing scope: accept this prerequisite repair with the disclosed transaction and recovery boundary. Complete July-upgrade recovery remains a separate campaign gate; package rollback alone is not claimed to reverse database migrations.

Related: #149705 documents the separate M2 product repairs and fixes the harness's false-success summaries and discarded migration diagnostics. M10 does not duplicate those product repairs.

## Evidence

- Exact-head hosted CI passed at `1340a76c3aba76dd890e02add1f049556ac1218c`: [CI run 35082452718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35082452718). No failed-run reruns were used.
- Rebase at `1340a76c3aba76dd890e02add1f049556ac1218c` preserves both patches unchanged. A serial single-worker A/B of the previously timed-out plugin-deferral case passed twice on pre-rebase head `6f5067b2dc7` and twice on the rebased head. Alternating case times were 56.120s / 85.323s / 26.195s / 21.632s; wall times were 465.743s / 320.485s / 191.390s / 124.887s. One-minute host load before/after each run was 92.96→92.09 / 68.51→107.74 / 118.67→134.67 / 147.21→104.04. The 120-second failure did not reproduce on either head; hosted exact-head CI subsequently passed for the rebased candidate.
- Fixture follow-up at `6f5067b2dc7cdc724e2dd41f537a3b435cf61ee7`: the Doctor input mock now imports the real schema-repair binding while retaining its existing migration stub. Both previously failing input cases pass. All 86 tests across the input, state-migration, plugin-deferral, plugin-persistence, and registry-snapshot suites passed; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` and `git diff --check` passed. Production code and assertions are unchanged by this follow-up.
- Both published updaters reproduced the original `audit-events-v2` failure against `180d1a0a6c68469ed0e5319d7325a1826aced7f1` in base, SQLite-volume, and legacy-operator-state/managed-restart rows.
- The regression uses the existing published `v2026.7.1-2` SQLite fixture with registered Doctor preflight options. It fails before this fix and passes afterward, preserving the audit record and pending plugin inputs.
- 61 focused schema/Doctor tests passed; the final persistence extraction passed 39 affected tests. Changed-file checks, build, package integrity, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh isolated Codex branch review was scoped-clean at P1.
- Candidate `43817c4b91d66cde0cfddd9643a80ae091029954` tarball SHA-256: `198c01e33c2dc47dea2d5de74fb8966b094b9fb662814cf355b5303f82395a73`. All workloads used one AWS Crabbox lease, isolated Docker state, and the mock provider.

| Baseline | Scenario / restart | Original candidate | Fixed candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.7.1-2 | base / manual | fail: audit-events-v2 | fail: Doctor 0, post-core 0; legacy plugin config remains |
| 2026.7.1-2 | sqlite-volume / manual | fail: audit-events-v2 | fail: Schema repaired; Doctor refuses deferred session receipt |
| 2026.7.1-2 | legacy-operator-state / auto-auth | fail: audit-events-v2 | fail: Doctor 0, post-core 0; Gateway 78; outage ≥78.9s |
| 2026.7.1-1 | base / manual | fail: audit-events-v2 | fail: Doctor 0, post-core 0; legacy plugin config remains |
| 2026.7.1-1 | sqlite-volume / manual | fail: audit-events-v2 | fail: Schema repaired; Doctor refuses deferred session receipt |
| 2026.7.1-1 | legacy-operator-state / auto-auth | fail: audit-events-v2 | fail: Doctor 0, post-core 0; Gateway 78; outage ≥79.2s |

End-to-end health, cron continuity, and rollback are not claimed for rows that stop at earlier assertions. Manual rows do not measure service downtime. Full logs, summaries, and diagnostic bundles are retained in the campaign evidence directory.

Exact base-row harness command; the other rows change the baseline, scenario, restart mode, and corresponding evidence paths:

```sh
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_BASELINE_SPEC=2026.7.1-2 \
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_PUBLISHED_BASELINE=1 \
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_SCENARIO=base \
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_UPDATE_RESTART_MODE=manual \
OPENCLAW_CURRENT_PACKAGE_TGZ=/tmp/matrix-L10-fixed-package/openclaw-candidate.tgz \
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_SUMMARY_JSON=/tmp/matrix-L10-fixed-evidence/2026.7.1-2/base/artifacts/summary.json \
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_ARTIFACT_DIR=/tmp/matrix-L10-fixed-evidence/2026.7.1-2/base/artifacts \
OPENCLAW_DOCKER_ALL_LOG_DIR=/tmp/matrix-L10-fixed-evidence/2026.7.1-2/base/published-diagnostics \
OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_LIVE_OPENAI=0 \
bash scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh
```

Volume and legacy rows use the same harness image with the existing `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`, selected by `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_E2E_IMAGE=openclaw-upgrade-survivor-trace OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1`. Default 900-second command and 1,200-second Docker timeouts remain unchanged.

LOC split: production **+74/-27** (net +47), tests **+59/-3** (net +56), docs **+4/-0**. Growth supplies the early canonical schema step and typed identity handoff; no new option, environment contract, dependency, schema, suppression, or baseline exception.
